name: Jājigrāma
location: By the Kāṭwā–Bardhamān light railway, 2 miles from Kāṭwā station
about:
Śrīpāṭa of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya. Here he first married Īśvarī Devī (Draupadī), daughter of Gopāla Cakravartī of this village. Gopāla dāsa later moved to Faridpur near Cākhandi (Murshidabad); his descendants live here.
There are the Madana-gopāla worshipped by Śrīnivāsa's son Gati Govinda, a śālagrāma, two trees planted by Śrīnivāsa and two stones on which he used to sit. A festival is held on Kārtika Gopāṣṭamī (also at Cākhandi).

name: Kāñcanagaḍiyā
location: Within a mile of Bājārsāhu station
about:
1. Śrīpāṭa of Dvija Haridāsa Ācārya. His two sons Śrīdāsa and Gokula Dāsa lived here: two of the «six Cakravartīs», disciples of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya. When Dvija Haridāsa left his body in Vṛndāvana his bones were brought here and given samādhi. Tirobhāva: Māgha kṛṣṇa ekādaśī. The service of Śrī Mohanarāya continues. Gokula Dāsa's descendants now live at Vaidyapura (Kāṭwā) and Śrīdāsa's at Sāṭui near Belḍāṅgā.
2. Śrīpāṭa of Rādhāvallabha Dāsa Maṇḍala, who translated Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī's Vilāpa-kusumāñjali.
3. Also connected with Vṛndāvana, a disciple of Śrīnivāsa.

name: Āṭapura
aka: Atapur, Antpur, Taḍā-Āṭapura, Tara Atpur, Āchurabāṭī
location: 5 minutes from Āṭapura station (Hāoḍā–Āmtā / Cāṁpāḍāṅgā light railway)
about: Śrīpāṭa of Parameśvara Dāsa Ṭhākura, one of the twelve gopālas. Deities: Śyāmasundara, Rādhā-Gopīnātha and Gaurāṅga. An old bakula and a kadamba tree grow together; the bakula is said to have sprung from his tooth-stick. His samādhi is here, and an old cymbal used in saṅkīrtana (perhaps Nityānanda Prabhu's), set beside the samādhi on his tirobhāva festival, Vaiśākha pūrṇimā.

name: Budhurī
location: One mile south-west of Bhagavāngolā station
about:
Śrīpāṭa of Rāmacandra Kavirāja and of Govinda Kavirāja (their maternal grandfather was Dāmodara Kavirāja; they lived before at Kumāranagara near Kheturi, Rājaśāhī). There are Govinda Kavirāja's Śrī Gopāla, two deities of Mahāprabhu installed by his descendants Ghanaśyāma and Haridāsa, and a Śyāmakuṇḍa and Rādhākuṇḍa dedicated by Śrīnivāsa Ācārya.
Also the śrīpāṭa of Ravi Rāya the pūjārī (disciple of Śrīnivāsa), of Gopīramaṇa, and of Balarāma Kavipati (disciple of Śyāmānanda).
Tirobhāva of Rāmacandra Kavirāja: Kārtika kṛṣṇa aṣṭamī; of Govinda Kavirāja: Āśvina śukla pratipat.

name: Saptagrāma
about: Śrīpāṭa of Uddhāraṇa Datta Ṭhākura. Once a great and rich port: «Saptagrāma» meant seven villages (Saptagrāma, Vaṁśavāṭī, Śivapura, Vāsudevapura, Kṛṣṇapura, Nityānandapura and Śaṅkhanagara); Triveṇī was part of it. The Pathans plundered it in 1592, and when the Sarasvatī river dried up (1632) the port was ruined.

name: Māliháṭi
location: 12 kroś south of Baharampur, north of Kāṭwā
about:
Śrīpāṭa of Rādhāmohana Ṭhākura, great-great-grandson of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya, guru of Mahārāja Nandakumāra and of Rāja Ravīndranārāyaṇa of Puṭiyā. A padakartā, he compiled the Padāmṛta-samudra; he defeated the court paṇḍitas of Jayasiṁha of Jaipur and established the parakīyā doctrine before Murshid Kuli Khān (1718). His seat, gadi and guesthouse are here; his disciples included Gokulānanda and Vaiṣṇava dāsa.
Also the śrīpāṭa of Yadunandana dāsa, disciple of Śrīnivāsa's daughter Hemalatā Devī and author of the Karṇānanda. Rādhāmohana's brother Yādavendra Ṭhākura lived at Dakṣiṇakhaṇḍa nearby.

name: Varāhanagara
about:
Pāṭa and samādhi of Bhāgavatācārya (Raghunātha Paṇḍita). The lost śrīpāṭa was recovered by a dream: two brothers of Bāgbāzār, Kālīprasāda and Parāṇa Cakravartī, were told to dig east of the pond where a snake would come out — that was the Ācārya's samādhi — to build a temple and install Gaura-Nityānanda on the next Māgha pūrṇimā (Viṣṇupriyā-patrikā).
The town is named after a siddha called Varāha; Portuguese, Dutch and English traders later lived here.

name: Khānākula
location: On the bank of the Dvārakeśvara river
about: Śrīpāṭa of Abhirāma Gopāla Ṭhākura (see also «Kṛṣṇanagara» in the Abhidhāna).

name: Jhāmaṭapura (Bardhamān)
location: Three miles from Gaṅgāṭikurī; Bāharāṇ halt (flag station), then 5–6 minutes to the śrīpāṭa
about: Śrīpāṭa of Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī. In the temple: Gaura-Nitāi, the Kavirāja Gosvāmī's wooden sandals, an old manuscript on palm leaves, and in a small shrine the footprints of Nityānanda Prabhu, who gave him darśana here (and, it is said, initiation, at the «Jagannātha ākhaḍā» at the edge of the village). Samādhi of a former mahānta, Gosāi dāsa Bābājī. Festival on the dvādaśī after Vijayā-daśamī.

name: Jhāmaṭapura (Hugli)
about: Śrīpāṭa of Yadunandana Ācārya, father-in-law of Vīrabhadra Prabhu (Vīrabhadra married his daughter Nārāyaṇī Devī), of Gaṅgādāsa Paṇḍita and of Śyāmadāsa Kavirāja.

name: Kenduli
location: From Śivapura, two miles on foot to the Ajaya river; Kenduli bāzār is on the other bank
about: Śrīpāṭa of Jayadeva, who used to visit the court of Lakṣmaṇa Sena; his father was Bhojadeva and his mother Vāmādevī. He found the deity of Rādhā-Mādhava in the Ajaya river, and later went with his wife to Vṛndāvana. West of Kendubilva are the ruins of Bilvamaṅgala's home.

name: Khaḍadaha
location: Temple two miles west of Khaḍadaha station (Eastern Railway), near the Gaṅgā
about: Residence of Nityānanda Prabhu with Vasudhā and Jāhnavā. The temple of Śyāmasundara (brick inscription of 1673 Śaka, by the artisan Rāmabhadra dāsa); the deity was carved from the stone brought by Vīrabhadra Prabhu. Vīrabhadra and Gaṅgā Devī were born here: a large platform with two tulasī-mañcas marks the birth room. Śrīnivāsa Ācārya and Narottama Ṭhākura came here. The ponds north-east of the temple are called Śvetagaṅgā and Yamunā.
